title: Wire one registry, override store, and session state through runtime
objective: Inject the same authoritative Manager, policy/override store, session identity, catalog cursor, and loaded ledger into commands, loop, SkillTool, and engines.
context: Complete one low-conflict slice of the accepted live skill catalog and cache-preserving design.
The worktree is shared and dirty; only owned_files may be modified.

source_evidence.note: Developer-context initial catalog and progressive disclosure inspiration.
Live discovery, visibility overrides, and skill lifecycle inspiration.

include: Create dependencies once at composition boundaries.
Route session meta state into each QueryLoop and SkillTool.
Restore session overlays/cursors on resume and persist updated state.
Create exactly one MemorySessionOverrideLayer, FileOverrideStore, Manager, and SkillTool; retarget the project store at workspace/session switches without replacing the shared Manager identity.
Atomically replace the Manager's project-source directories at an active workspace switch while preserving user/plugin/managed sources, so old project skills cannot leak into the new catalog.
Restore a session's complete override map atomically, and persist session skill metadata through project-scoped session adapters without exposing a partially restored overlay.

Inject a visible-history-aware loaded-ledger resolver: before each model or explicit-user invocation, strictly absorb current full/superseding user invocation envelopes already present in the current context epoch, then return the authoritative ledger state to SkillTool.

The loaded-ledger resolver must never call Manager because SkillTool invokes it inside Manager.ResolveLatest; model calls use ToolExecutionContext Messages and exact project/session identity, while explicit UI calls resolve an exact idle conversation or fail closed.

Preserve complete message identity and developer/provenance metadata when ToolExecutionContext defensively clones messages; deep-copy mutable content maps/slices so resolver evidence cannot be dropped or raced.
Never let a pending UI result, malformed lookalike, stale/revoked body, another epoch, or an envelope not actually present in QueryLoop history establish loaded evidence.
Inject the shared skills menu launcher and mutation backend so interactive toggles use the same registry and override store as text commands.
Keep Skill tool schema and prompt cache key stable across catalog changes.
exclude: Do not modify production files owned by another task.
Do not add dependencies or perform unrelated refactors.

implementation_steps: Replace disconnected or duplicate manager creation sites.
Add project-scoped skills metadata load/save methods to both session adapters and restore only state reconciled against current visible history.
Wire the same origin-user SkillTool adapter plus dynamic language/session/loaded-ledger resolvers into TUI and screen-reader configurations.
Add an integration-style wiring test with two sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Command, query loop, and SkillTool observe the same registry revision.
Two sessions share discovery but not session overlays or ledgers.
Resume restores the correct session state.
Session override restore is atomic, and project-scoped metadata load/save never follows a mutable global current-project pointer.

A workspace switch preserves the shared Manager pointer but replaces project-source directories and project override settings atomically enough that the next snapshot contains no skills from the prior project.
Loaded-ledger resolution cannot re-enter Manager or deadlock behind a queued Manager writer.
Model tool calls resolve from their immutable ToolExecutionContext messages; an absent, mismatched, running, or ambiguous project/session conversation fails closed to a full envelope.

A successful explicit user invocation becomes eligible for an already-loaded acknowledgement only after its exact envelope is present in visible QueryLoop history; rejected or invisible results never do.
The interactive list and text command observe the same effective state, mutation result, and revision.

risks: Owned composition files are dirty; preserve existing fork/goal/presentation wiring.
Engine conversation identity is project plus session while the Manager API is session-only; duplicate session IDs across projects must fail closed instead of silently sharing overlays.
Never hold CoreEngine conversation locks while acquiring Manager or override-store locks; SkillTool already holds Manager while calling the runtime resolver.
dispatch_prompt: Wire a single live skill registry and scoped session state through runtime composition. Keep resolver callbacks Manager-free, route model calls by ToolExecutionContext, restore session overrides atomically, use project-scoped metadata adapters, and inject the same origin-user SkillTool into TUI and screen-reader surfaces. Do not implement UI or alter unrelated component internals.
